guard: a second top-level session gets its own emitter, and the session it replaces is drained and closed on the wire first
why: THE HOLDER'S REFUSAL IS CORRECT AND IS NOT THE TARGET HERE. A holder binds to one thread and
refuses a second terminally, because the write-ahead log is keyed to the thread. The defect was
the caller: the plugin adopted every top-level session into the SAME holder, so `/new` killed it
and the plane went dark with nothing on the wire to say so. These mutations put the caller back
into each of the three states it was in or could regress to.
R1 is the shipped defect: no swap, so the second session is adopted into the bound holder.
R2 and R3 are the two halves of the drain, which are what an external observer sees: without the
flush the tail the old session had settled never reaches the subject, and without the close the
observer is left holding a run that never ends.
The ordering barrier between the two chains is NOT registered as a mutation. Removing it is a
race rather than a defect that reproduces on demand, and a mutation whose kill depends on
scheduling would report SURVIVED on a slow machine and read as a hole in the suite.
R4 REGISTERS THE ORDERING RACE, which the note above declined to register. What changed is that the
interleave was measured rather than assumed: the plugin bus dispatches with `void hook.event(...)`,
so a second create lands mid-drain deterministically here rather than by luck, and the mutant was
observed to redden on the named assertion across repeated runs. If it ever reports SURVIVED, the
honest reading is that this harness stopped reaching the window, not that the guard is optional.

mutations.name: R1 the second top-level session is adopted into the bound holder, which is the state this connector shipped in
R2 the drain closes the old session without flushing what it had already settled
mutations.expectRed: order:and the tail it was still holding went out BEFORE that close

mutations.name: R3 the drain leaves the old session's run open, so an observer holds a run that never ends
mutations.expectRed: order:every run the first session OPENED was closed

mutations.name: R4 the swap is no longer serialized, so two creates inside one drain window both retire the same holder
mutations.expectRed: race:the holder the FIRST of two racing creates installed is retired, exactly once
mutations.note: Chaining every swap off an ALREADY-RESOLVED promise removes the serialization while leaving the code compiling, which is the smallest expression of the defect. Under it both invocations capture the same holder to retire, the first replacement is adopted (its write-ahead log opens) and is then overwritten, and the session it held leaves a run open on the subject forever.
mutations.cell: race:the holder the FIRST of two racing creates installed is retired, exactly once (and the session they both replace is retired ONCE, not drained twice)
